title: Composition isomorphism of derived pullbacks of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$, $g\colon Y\to Z$ morphisms of schemes. There is a natural isomorphism
$$
L(g\circ f)^*\cong Lf^*\circ Lg^*\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Z})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})
$$
of derived pullbacks ([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]), induced by the underived composition isomorphism $(g\circ f)^*\cong f^*\circ g^*$ of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp].

proof.text: Put $h=g\circ f$, $\mathcal A_T=\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$, $F_a=a^*$ and $L_a=La^*$ for $a=f,g,h$. These are the full module-object pullbacks and their total left derived functors of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], not functors on abelian sheaves alone. By [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], each $F_a$ is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits, for every commutative condensed $\Lambda$ and every scheme morphism $a$. Let $Q_T:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A_T)\to D(\mathcal A_T)$ be the localization at quasi-isomorphisms of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in the chosen universes. Write $C(F_a)$ for application of $F_a$ to every term and differential. For $a:T\to S$, the total left derived functor $L_a$ comes with its structure transformation $\epsilon_a:L_aQ_S\to Q_TC(F_a)$, and $(L_a,\epsilon_a)$ is a right Kan extension of $Q_TC(F_a)$ along $Q_S$; this is the meaning of a (total) left derived functor used in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor].

source.place: First sentence: exactness of all pullbacks and the total left derived functors

proof.text: For $a:T\to S$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] says that $C(F_a)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and supplies $D_a:D(\mathcal A_S)\to D(\mathcal A_T)$ with a natural isomorphism $\varphi_a:D_aQ_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_TC(F_a)$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] makes $(D_a,\varphi_a)$ a total left derived pair. Compare it with the total left derived pair $(L_a,\epsilon_a)$ from step 1, using the right Kan universal property. It gives unique maps $u_a:L_a\to D_a$, $v_a:D_a\to L_a$ with $\varphi_a(u_aQ_S)=\epsilon_a$ and $\epsilon_a(v_aQ_S)=\varphi_a$. Substitution gives $\varphi_a(u_av_aQ_S)=\varphi_a$ and $\epsilon_a(v_au_aQ_S)=\epsilon_a$, so the same uniqueness gives $u_av_a=1$ and $v_au_a=1$. Thus $u_a$ is the canonical natural isomorphism $L_a\cong D_a$, and $p_a:=\varphi_a(u_aQ_S):L_aQ_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_TC(F_a)$ is natural and invertible on every complex. No boundedness or preservation of K-flat objects by a second pullback is required.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), exact-functor principle; left-derived version and its Kan uniqueness are supplied by the cited existing node

proof.text: Take exactly the underived natural isomorphism $b:F_h\xrightarrow{\sim}F_fF_g$ of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. On a cochain complex $K$ in $\mathcal A_Z$, the maps $b_{K^n}$ form a chain isomorphism $B_K:C(F_h)K\xrightarrow{\sim}C(F_f)C(F_g)K$: its chain-map equation is $F_fF_g(d_K^n)b_{K^n}=b_{K^{n+1}}F_h(d_K^n)$, the naturality of $b$ at $d_K^n$. Its inverse is given degreewise by $b_{K^n}^{-1}$. Naturality at each component of a chain map proves that $B$ is natural in $K$.

source.place: Second sentence: induce the comparison of levelwise functors from the specified underived isomorphism

proof.text:
For $K\in\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A_Z)$ put $q_K=p_{f,C(F_g)K}\circ L_f(p_{g,K})$. It is a natural isomorphism from $L_fL_gQ_ZK$ to $Q_XC(F_f)C(F_g)K$. Consequently
$$t_K=q_K^{-1}\circ Q_X(B_K)\circ p_{h,K}:L_hQ_ZK\xrightarrow{\sim}L_fL_gQ_ZK$$
is a natural isomorphism of functors on cochain complexes. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] with localization $Q_Z$, target $D(\mathcal A_X)$, and the functors $L_h$ and $L_fL_g$. Their composites with $Q_Z$ invert quasi-isomorphisms since $Q_Z$ inverts them and functors preserve inverses. With the comparison isomorphisms identities, that clause descends $t$ to a natural transformation $c:L_h\to L_fL_g$ with $c_{Q_ZK}=t_K$. Descend $t^{-1}$ in the same way. Since descent respects composition and identities, the descended transformations are inverse, so $c$ is a natural isomorphism. Its defining equation
$$q_K\circ c_{Q_ZK}=Q_X(B_K)\circ p_{h,K}$$
identifies it as the comparison induced by the specified $b$ under the canonical exact-derived identifications. Clause (3) of the same localization node makes a transformation with these components unique. This proves the claimed ambient comparison on unbounded derived categories.

source.place: Second and third sentences: descent of the degreewise comparison and transport along the canonical exact-derived identifications
